subject: gk
question: The concepts of Dhamma was popularized by which of the following Mauryan kings?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka.**__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• **Ashoka was the great Mauryan ruler and grandson of the dynasty's founder Chandragupta Maurya.**
 
• Ashoka became a Buddhist in the 9th year of his reign i.e., a year after the conquest of Kalinga.
 
• **Dhamma is the Prakrit form of the Sanskrit word 'Dharma'.**
 
• Ashoka’s dhamma was neither a new religion nor a new political philosophy, it was a way of life.
 
• Ashoka denounced all useless ceremonies and sacrifices held under the influence of superstition.
 
• One of the striking features of Asoka’s edicts is that he regards himself as a father figure for the people. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• Ashoka's major dhamma is inscribed in 14 rock edicts. Some of the important dhamma are:
 
 
• Prohibition of animal sacrifices in festive and public gatherings.
 
• It pleads for toleration amongst all religions.
 
• Respect for others and regard even for slaves and servants and donations to sramanas and Brahmans.
 
• Emphatic plea for toleration amongst the various religions.
 
• Plantation of medicinal herbs and trees and the digging of wells along the roads, describes the promotion of the welfare of the people.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• ** Bindusara was Ashoka's father**, who expanded the Mauryan empire but did not promote Dhamma as actively as his son. 
 
• **Dasaratha was a Mauryan emperor **who preceded Bindusara and was known for his military campaigns against the Greeks and other regional powers.
 
• Chandragupta was the founder of the Mauryan dynasty and Ashoka's grandfather, who established a vast empire but did not leave as much of a cultural or religious legacy as his descendants.
